summary: Router 0.20.0 narrows two paths for shared-memory poisoning (TM-10). ADR-0060: router.memory_scopes.<scope>.writers lists the clients that may write a shared scope; shared_config.parse_scopes validates it (list, at most 64 distinct nonempty names without control characters), config.py refuses an unknown writer name and any write grant on the scope whose client is not listed, naming client and scope; absent or empty means nobody may write. memory.scope_for_principal checks the list again for every write, so a live policy cannot widen it; reading and deletion are unchanged. ADR-0059: memory.prepare skips automatic recall when the request body carries a nonempty tools list (native, OpenAI and Anthropic shapes after conversion) and the project grant does not set recall_into_tools: true; the state skipped:tools is reported in X-Skirnir-Memory-State and the journal and counted. recall_into_tools is a boolean in PROJECT_FIELDS (schema derived) that requires read. Explicit recall APIs are unchanged. Breaking for configurations that grant writes on a shared scope: they must add writers; the documentation, example config, changelog, threat model and risk register describe it.

findings.evidence: Automatic recall inserted shared facts, possibly written by another client, into requests that offered tools; any client grant with write on a shared scope made that client a writer without a change on the scope.
findings.resolution: Recall into tool requests only by explicit grant opt-in, and two-sided writer rights checked at load and per request. A listed writer can still plant false facts and an opted-in client depends on its own tool confirmation, so TM-10 stays open.

tests.command: router.py --check --pure against a configuration with and without writers
tests.evidence: With writers: configuration ok. Without: 'client ... may write memory scope ... only if memory_scopes....writers lists it' (rc 2).

limitations: The router cannot see whether a client confirms tool calls; an opted-in client's tool behavior is outside unit-test coverage.
A listed writer is trusted to write correct facts; the list limits who may write, not what.
